clue.text: Boast by council levying only 1% of the rateable value

parts.note: a penny in the pound is one per cent, and P is the abbreviation for penny
a rate is the local tax a council levies on a property's rateable value

explanation.surface: A thrifty council boasts of charging almost nothing in local tax.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'penny rate', one penny in the pound or 1%, was a familiar phrase when British councils levied rates (a property tax), so P + RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to talk idly and at length, often boastfully, so it can stand for brag.

clue.text: The sound of a footfall is plain in the Soviet Union

indicators.note: the clue asks for what a word sounds like when spoken, a homophone signal

parts.note: a footfall is a single step

explanation.surface: Footsteps echo across a flat Soviet landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppes are the vast treeless grasslands of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Cast out a demon or cast away

indicators.note: to cast is also to throw into a new shape, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An exorcist either drives out a demon or throws it overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' sounds like exorcism, but it reshapes the letters of A DEMON OR; 'cast away' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is left stranded on an island, just as a marooned sailor is.

clue.text: Resign if the car parked in front won't move

definitions.text: if the car parked in front won't move

explanation.surface: A driver blocked in by another car gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from a commitment is to back out; and a blocked car must reverse, or back, out of the space.

clue.text: Vegetable species that has been evolved?

definitions.text: Vegetable species that has been evolved?

parts.words: Vegetable species that has been evolved?
parts.note: in mathematics evolution is the extraction of a root, so a species that has been evolved is read as one grown from a root

explanation.surface: A botanist wonders about a vegetable bred over generations.
explanation.walkthrough: Old mathematics called finding a root 'evolution', the inverse of involution (raising to a power); here that sense meets the crop grown for its root, such as turnips or carrots.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips, carrots and swedes are farmed for their edible underground parts.

clue.text: Novel system of backing a copier to produce a journal

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the basis on which bets are settled, a betting or backing system
an aper is one who apes, a copier

explanation.surface: A new method of supporting a photocopier is used to print a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' here means betting on horses, where SP stands for starting price; an APER is one who apes, i.e. copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily paper is a journal of the day's news.

clue.text: Compile a letter immediately by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue tells us the answer is how a phrase would sound when spoken

explanation.surface: Someone is told to draft a letter at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To write away is to send off by post, as in writing away for a brochure.

clue.text: A lot of wicked brewers use centigrade heating device

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for centigrade
an oven is a device for heating food

explanation.surface: A gang of malevolent beer-makers relies on a thermometer and stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wicked brewers' are witches stirring cauldrons, not beer-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of witches, who brew potions, is traditionally thirteen strong.

clue.text: Come down to earth

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stop daydreaming and be realistic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touches down when it arrives; and soil or ground is also called this.

clue.text: Knock off a set of pipes to operate

parts.note: an organ stop is a set of pipes of one tone
to operate is to work, as a machine works

explanation.surface: An organist finishes playing the pipes and goes off to do a job.
explanation.walkthrough: An organ stop controls one rank of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off is slang for finishing the day's labour and downing tools.

clue.text: One who draws his 2ls

clue.text: Forest valley

explanation.surface: A woodland lies in a dale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Dean is a woodland in Gloucestershire, England; and a dean, or dene, is a narrow wooded vale.

clue.text: Out of form, but not on a course apparently

explanation.surface: A golfer playing badly is not even on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means unwell or off form; on a golf course, scoring below the standard figure is the same phrase.

clue.text: Bid for a driver with three irons?

explanation.surface: A golfer bids for a set of four clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a bid names a number and a suit; in golf a driver and three irons are four clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract call in the card game bridge; and a driver plus three irons make that many golf sticks.

clue.text: Chest of regimental com with end of recognition

clue.text: What the army did after spilling over the enemy

definitions.text: What the army did after spilling over the enemy

parts.words: What the army did after spilling over the enemy
parts.note: an army clears up remaining resistance after overrunning a foe, while spilling suggests wiping up a liquid mess

explanation.surface: Soldiers clean up after a battle that swept across enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilling over' suggests a liquid spill wiped up with a cloth, but it also means the army surging over the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who finish off scattered resistance are said to clear it up, the same phrase used for wiping a spill.

clue.text: Could it be made from Western Region paper if torn?

definitions.text: Could it be made from Western Region paper if torn?

parts.note: WR stood for the Western Region of British Railways

indicators.note: paper that is torn up has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cover could be made from torn railway paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Western Region was one of the regions of nationalised British Railways; 'if torn' rearranges PAPER into APPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover or packaging made of paper is exactly this.

clue.text: Dash good advice if you want a parliamentary seat

definitions.text: good advice if you want a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: A would-be politician is told to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee in a hurry; and to stand as a candidate is to run for election.

clue.text: Poet going from bank to bank

explanation.surface: A poet strolls along a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913; and spans crossing rivers carry you between banks.

clue.text: Fall down when disembarking?

explanation.surface: A passenger stumbles while leaving a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to lose your footing; and when you get off, the journey is finished.

clue.text: It is seen as an opinion

explanation.surface: Something visible is taken as a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista or sight is what is seen; and a personal standpoint on a question is also this.

clue.text: Grass irritation?

explanation.surface: A lawn causes annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass is slang for a police informer; and to annoy someone is to irritate them, in British slang.

clue.text: Bit of a swine, and more impetuous

explanation.surface: Someone is rather a pig and too hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon comes from a pig; and someone more reckless is the comparative of hasty.

clue.text: Spirited despite being strapped

explanation.surface: A lively person is tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink spiked with alcohol has been given spirit; and boots tied with cords are fastened.

clue.text: Where secrets may be kept up to provide army cover

definitions.text: Where secrets may be kept up

explanation.surface: Military secrets are kept safe under protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' is read as 'of the arm': a cover for an arm. 'Up one's sleeve' means kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan kept up one's cuff is hidden; and a garment's arm section covers the arm.

clue.text: Book which, for Saxon veomen, meant a time of reckoning

explanation.surface: For Saxon farmers, a register meant judgement day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Domesday Book, William the Conqueror's 1086 survey of England, was nicknamed after the Last Judgement because its verdicts could not be appealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1086 survey of England was named after the Last Judgement, the final day of reckoning.

clue.text: A handy contest — roughly

parts.note: a boxing bout is a contest fought with the hands

explanation.surface: A fistfight is a bit rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' means fought with the hands: a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately and around are both ways to say roughly.

clue.text: Genius adopts metric unit to measure length of border

indicators.note: the spirit takes on the unit as its addition, placing it after itself

parts.note: a genius is a guardian spirit, and a peri is a Persian fairy spirit
a meter is the American spelling of the metric unit of length

explanation.surface: A clever person uses a metric measure to gauge a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genius' looks like a clever person, but here it is a guardian spirit, as in genius loci; 'adopts' means the spirit takes the unit on behind it. The unit takes its American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance around the edge of a shape is its boundary length.
